articles.title: The Death of Corporate Accountability and the Novel That Could Save Western Civilization
articles.bodyHtml:
We've all heard the chantings of the people out in the streets these past few days, a red-hot anger that seeps through our pavements, cobblestones and zebra crossings. We, as a society, have been shown yet again that corporations are above the laws-- laws that should be the foundation of our country, laws that should carry us all on their calloused, muscle-y shoulders and make us proud of how far we have come as a civilization.

It makes you want to weep, fall to your knees, shake your fist to the skies and exclaim, "Why?!"

I can envision the top shots behind Arbule Corp. standing in their tall glass towers, clinking glasses, laughing and both literally and figuratively looking down at the masses parading outside their headquarters. What can they do? What power do they have to overthrow the leaders and visionaries behind this corrupt corporation when they are the ones calling the shots?

"In its majestic equality, the law forbids rich and poor alike to sleep under bridges, beg in the streets and steal loaves of bread."
— Anatole France, The Red Lily (1894), Chapter VII.

We could have an endless debate, going around in circles like fish in an ever-lowering pond, until we lie there in the sludge and mud, gasping for air and wiggling helplessly under the scorching sun, arguing about the positives and negatives of tort reform.
We all know this is going nowhere.

Now, imagine that there was a book-- a book of the highest intellectual caliber, with knowledge and truths between every page, that could end this debate once and for all.

The Holy Grail. A myth.

Imagine.

What if I told you that this myth, a myth of great importance, like the Round Table of King Arthur's court or Emperors Nero's own fiddle-- still smelling of smoke, a witness to the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, was no myth at all?

I truly believe that my book (yes!) could unite us again and overthrow the capitalist pigs in their glass towers. The old, dried but truthful ink of my old trusty typewriter, an enigma of machinery that has borne witness to countless heralded articles, read and loved by many, has been clacking away at this book for years. Its manuscript pages have almost yellowed with age, but the content remains just as fresh and young as the day.

I am well aware that I am teasing you, my dear reader(s), but alas, I cannot yet reveal the truth. Not without first finding a publisher who actually values the truth, who can see the raw contents and fully understand them just as they are, without endless pleading to change the meaning, erase the core of what the book is trying to convey, or censor what I believe is my life's greatest accomplishment.

And for that, I am afraid that the rage of the people will need to carry on for a while longer.

I will end this article with yet another quote that I find fitting to my situation,

"If liberty means anything at all it means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear."
— George Orwell, The Freedom of the Press, his proposed preface to Animal Farm (written 1945, published 1972)
articles.description: As public anger intensifies over corporate greed and the erosion of accountability, our columnist Mercedes Jorimara Fack-Bisbar examines the feelings of the general public, the limitations of tort reform and the extraordinary literary work that may hold the key to restoring peace to the Western civilization.

articles.title: The Silent Infiltration: How Communist Ideology Threatens Our Way of Life
articles.bodyHtml:
The dinner table, a scene that sparks joy and a sense of home for millions of people in our beautiful nation. The familiarity of the wooden surface, the soft clinking of cutlery and glasses, crinkling decorated tissues and the warm embrace of breaking bread amongst friends and family. 

A place that should feel safe.

Where we should be able to relax.
     To let the hectic and stressful day leave your
           shoulders and satisfying food enter your belly.

That safety has been taken from me.

It was a normal evening, just like the previous evening and the evenings before. I was seated at our grand oak table, candles lit, wine glasses filled and the vibrating expectancy of a juicy savoury steak being served in front of me.

But that moment never came. 

Instead, I was served a cold bowl, its bland, green content completely odourless, nothing to stimulate my culinary senses or enrich my mind. My husband smiled at me with an expectant look in his eyes, as if to say, "Gaze upon this glorious dish!" My knuckles whitening and the cutlery in my hand creaking and bending in my concealed wrath, I took a long, hard look at the man before me. 

For you see, Communism has infiltrated my dinner table. 

It had started slowly.
Short, innocent ads playing in our living room, depicting people cutting vegetables, chewing on carrot sticks and rows of perfect white teeth smiling while selling their products and promoting this lifestyle. Slowly it turned more sinister. A recent released documentary depicting the alleged horrors of the meat industry and the mass hysteria of munching grass instead of the grass-fed animals themselves spread like a wildfire throughout our nation. Banners, protesters and vegans en masse began hounding the everyday Joe and Jane, claiming more and more victims. 

It is preposterous! Humans have, since the time of our Lord and Saviour's birth, eaten meat, digesting the valuable nutrients that are required to make our bodies and muscles strong. Have we all suddenly forgotten that meat is an incredible source of protein? 

How are we, as a nation, supposed to be able to protect ourselves if our bodies wither away, the butcher and hunting industries collapse and with them the economy? Who could benefit from this?
The answer has been right in front of everyones eyes: a big glaring C from across our nation's borders, a tsunami waiting to happen. 

How do we stop this infiltration and the risk it poses to our nation's security? I throw my hands in the air; I have to admit and be honest here: I don't know. 

But I do know that it begins with the simple word "no."

And that was exactly what I told my husband, the bowl of grass turned upside down and laying on the floor. 

No.

authors.name: Mercedes Jorimara Fack-Bisbar
authors.bio: Mercedes Jorimara Fack-Bisbar is an esteemed political commentator, a cultural critic and a lifelong defender of Western civilization. With nearly four decades of experience in public discourse, Mrs. Fack-Bisbar has established herself as one of the nation's most uncompromising voices on matters of politics, morality and the increasingly concerning decline of traditional values.
